rationale: Obscure technical term identified with the New Man (ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣⲡⲉ) on this page. Has an icon (line 4) and exists 'in her' (the Virgin/body, line 1). Possibly 'the deposited one / the laid-up one' (from ⲕⲱ 'lay, place') or 'the firmly-set one' (from ⲧⲱⲕ). Functions as a synonym/alternate title for the cosmic-spiritual reality stored in the body-as-temple. Awaits parallels.

proposed_english: to blaze a path / to make a way
rationale: Verbal idiom: ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲟⲩ- ('a') + ϫⲁⲩ-ⲙⲁⲓⲧ ('way-setting'). Same root as ⲣⲉϩⲭⲁⲩⲙⲁⲓⲧ 'guide / path-setter' (in glossary). Used here of the Virgin of Light who blazes a path before the soul into the upper place.

Habitual 3sg.f form. Likely ϣⲁⲥ- + ⲃⲱⲗ-stem with assimilation. Antithetical pair-partner with ⲱⲁⲥⲱⲛϩ̄ 'she habitually lives' on the same page: in somatic/psychic registers the soul releases what is not hers; in pneumatic register she lives. Etymology not entirely certain.
Likely Lyc. nominal of ⲡⲱⲣⲭ/ⲡⲱⲣϫ 'separate, divide' (cf. ⲡⲱⲣⲭ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary). In vice-catalogue alongside ⲫⲑⲟⲛⲟⲥ 'envy' and ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲉⲃⲉ 'foolishness.'

proposed_english: from every life / from all (manner of) life
rationale: Possibly reduplicated ⲱⲛϩ̄-ⲱⲛϩ̄ 'every-life' or related to ⲍⲱⲱⲛ. Used of the Living Member redeemed forth from all manifestations of life into the body of the righteous one.

Lyc. variant of Sah. ⲙ̄ⲧⲟⲛ 'rest' (cf. accumulated ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲙ̄ⲧⲁⲛ 'place of rest,' ⲛⲁⲧⲉⲍⲟ 'unfailing rest'). Confirmed here in eschatological context: the catechumen asks whether rest comes to be for the deceased.
Title of the Virgin of Light (= the robe of the New Man), who is identified as both first and last. Manichaean eschatological-soteriological self-designation.
Lyc. variant of Sah. ϫⲱⲗⲕ 'draw, pull, set in array' (cf. accumulated ⲭⲱⲗⲕ̄ in similar register). Used here of the Virgin who draws the soul up to the height.
Lyc. qualitative of ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄ 'mingle, mix' (cf. ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ in glossary). The fortunes 'which are mingled with her' in the psychikon — same root as the eschatological-cosmological mingling vocabulary.
